title: UPDATE: Chinese AI Providers Now Hold All Top 5 Usage Spots on OpenRouter
summary:
DeepSeek's new V4.1 Flash model processed more than 35 trillion tokens in one week, a fourfold increase over the previous week, to become the most used AI tool on the OpenRouter aggregator. The volume surge helped Chinese AI providers capture all five of the top spots on the platform's usage rankings, including models from Zhipu, MiniMax, and Tencent. The shift highlights a growing trend of developers migrating to cheaper, more efficient models as the market for AI tokens becomes increasingly commoditized.

The rise of low-cost alternatives comes as growth in actual spending on high-end models remains uneven. While Anthropic's daily token volume on OpenRouter rose to an average of roughly 2.2 trillion by Oct. 24 following the launch of Opus 5.5, data from Ramp indicates that overall spending on the company's models is still 1.6% below its July peak. Despite the spending lag, Opus 5.5 now accounts for 63% of total spend on Anthropic, and some investors predict the company's year-end annualized revenue could surpass $100B as falling prices stimulate higher total compute demand.

Spend on Anthropic models remains 1.6% below its July peak, according to Ramp data.

Opus 5.5 now accounts for 63% of Anthropic spend, so frontier models do matter. The idea that AI is already "good enough" is probably overrated as a concern IMO.

But price cuts / competition at all intelligence levels are still the most significant threats to AI model companies, and continue to form cracks in the AI thesis.

selectedTweets.text:
The most used AI model in the world on OpenRouter right now is Chinese.

DeepSeek's new V4.1 Flash model processed more than 35 TRILLION tokens this week, up about 4X from the week before.

Its older version sits in second place, and the top five spots are all Chinese models from DeepSeek, Zhipu, MiniMax and Tencent.

Developers are choosing these models because they are good enough and extremely cheap.

This is exactly what happens when AI models become commodities.

Prices fall, usage explodes, and total compute demand goes up, not down.

That is bullish for the companies selling the chips, memory and power underneath all of it.
selectedTweets.quotedTweetText:
Anthropic token usage just went VERTICAL.

According to OpenRouter data, daily tokens for Anthropic models sat around 0.6 trillion a day on a 7 day average from June through mid September. Then Anthropic shipped Opus 5.5 on September 22, Sonnet 5.5 on September 28 and Haiku 5.5 on October 7. By October 24, the 7 day average had climbed above 2.2 trillion tokens a day, with single days peaking near 3 trillion. That is roughly 3.5x the summer baseline in about a month.

Token usage is the cleanest demand signal in AI. Every one of those tokens has to run on real chips in real data centers, and demand for compute keeps EXPLODING. That demand flows straight to Anthropic's compute partners like $AMZN, $GOOGL and $NVDA, and it is another reason the AI infrastructure buildout is nowhere near done.

selectedTweets.text:
Wouldn't be surprised if Anthropic revenue is reaccelerating in October.

OpenRouter usage has recovered sharply from August, with several recent days around 450–600B tokens.

In the most recent breakdown, Opus 5.5 accounts for 197B of the 361B tokens recorded so far. Fable 5.1 adds another 32B.

Together, almost 64% of usage.

At standard uncached pricing, Opus 5.5 costs twice as much as Sonnet 5.5, while Fable 5.1 costs five times as much.

Assuming the same input/output mix, Fable’s 32B tokens would therefore generate the same bill as approximately 160B Sonnet tokens.

There’s been a lot of concern recently about slowing growth at the frontier labs and whether revenues can keep up with spending on compute.

If Anthropic’s growth is picking up again, that would challenge an important part of the bearish case.

selectedTweets.quotedTweetText:
Here is what is going on with OpenAI/Anthropic:

-OpenAI quickly saw Anthropic’s success at the end of 2025 and pivoted resources to agentic coding

-By April, OpenAI’s products had largely caught up, with positive developer reception of its GPT-5.5 coding agent (the online vibes from top developers were clear then)

-By the July 9 release of GPT-5.6, you could argue OpenAI had surpassed Anthropic in capability. That led to several months in which OpenAI took material share from Anthropic, leading to a growth rate slowdown at Anthropic

-On Sept. 22, Anthropic released a much better model Opus 5.5, which I expect is sparking a rebound in Anthropic's business. And when Anthropic releases Fable 5.5 soon, ARR should re-accelerate into IPO

-OpenAI CFO on Bloomberg TV today said business momentum is continuing in Q4. The confusion surrounding FT’s OpenAI reporting (net effective impression on readers) last week has poisoned the sentiment well where market is largely ignoring every positive OpenAI business data point (which has been EXTREMELY STRONG since July 9)

-Over the next six to twelve months, I anticipate a close back-and-forth for model leadership between OpenAI and Anthropic. 

-The business revenue in aggregate for these two frontier AI model companies should continue to be incredible.
